briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 19, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Warning of Climate Catastrophe: Intensifying Extreme Weather Phenomena
sections.content: Today's briefing begins with a serious warning about extreme weather phenomena striking across the globe. Recently, deadly floods caused by glacial collapse in Nepal, Tibet, and China have resulted in over 1,400 deaths and massive property damage amounting to 3.6 trillion KRW, with anthropogenic climate change identified as a decisive factor [1, 24, 29, 34]. Meanwhile, as the world prepares for a 'super' El Niño phenomenon, research indicates that global warming is further intensifying its power, urging proactive government responses [32, 36]. Climate change also poses a direct threat to agricultural production and food security, with rivers drying up due to severe drought in Brazil, and U.S. wheat farmers facing uncertainty amidst drought and geopolitical turmoil [39, 40]. As such, climate change is generating rapidly accumulating hidden workplace costs and causing severe economic and social repercussions across society, including violence against those performing rain rituals in some parts of Africa [30, 33].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic and International Carbon Neutrality Goals and Policy Progress
sections.content: Amidst this crisis, diverse efforts continue both domestically and internationally to achieve carbon neutrality goals and respond to climate change. The Korea Climate Change Foundation has initiated the discovery of joint renewable energy and carbon reduction projects by expanding climate and energy cooperation with Kyrgyzstan [2, 9]. Domestically, local councils are strongly advocating for energy improvements in public facilities, emphasizing the seamless implementation of the 2050 carbon neutrality goal, and promoting proactive private sector participation. Active community-level movements, such as participation in environmental festivals for carbon neutrality practices, are also prevalent [3, 7, 8]. Furthermore, efforts to raise awareness through citizen participation and education are underway, including Seobu Power spreading carbon neutrality ideas through education and Yeosu City conducting sharing events with the Carbon Neutrality Practice Alliance [4, 6]. Internationally, governments and institutions are also strengthening their preparedness for climate change; for example, the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency announced a 'Comprehensive Climate Action Plan' to achieve 'net-zero' emissions, and the Philadelphia Water Department is preparing for extreme weather events [25, 27]. In Canada, a booklet providing reliable guidance on climate change information has been published for citizens, and climate caravans are urging stronger climate action, continuing information sharing and calls for action [35, 37].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Innovative Approaches
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy, a core element in overcoming the climate crisis, is accelerating both domestically and internationally. The Korean government is closely managing large-scale solar projects through an inter-ministerial task force, accelerating towards achieving 100GW of renewable energy. Financial institutions like Saemaul Undong Credit Cooperatives are also actively supporting renewable energy and social housing, expanding aid through social solidarity finance [11, 14, 21]. Bangladesh is also providing low-interest financing for rooftop solar, and the European Union (EU) is demonstrating a leading role, with renewable energy already accounting for 54% of its total electricity generation [15, 16]. To enhance the social acceptance of renewable energy generation projects, strategies for distributed power sources with community profit-sharing models and proposals for introducing renewable energy pensions are emerging. Technological innovation is also active, with initiatives such as building eco-friendly data centers utilizing water from Daecheong Dam, KEPCO KDN's cooperation in Indonesia's new and renewable energy projects, and solving energy poverty issues through the combination of grid-forming and AI technology [12, 17, 19, 22, 23]. Furthermore, efforts to develop the overall renewable energy industry ecosystem are continuing, including the publication of new books on carbon-neutral fuels and energy issues, projections for market growth, and mentoring and support programs for workforce development [5, 10, 13, 18, 20].

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges and Policy Difficulties in Climate Change Response
sections.content: Despite the importance of responding to climate change, policy difficulties and challenges still persist. Some political movements, such as the U.S. Trump administration's Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) repealing power plant pollution limits, raise concerns that they could undermine climate change mitigation efforts [26]. In Australia, major polluting industries are overly reliant on carbon offsets in their climate crisis commitments, drawing criticism that this raises questions about the system's reliability and is akin to a 'sandcastle' [41]. Furthermore, in the political sphere, diverse stances are presented by climate and energy-related candidates, or candidates supporting unsubstantiated claims are running, suggesting difficulties in achieving a unified approach and strong policy implementation for climate change [31, 38]. These factors indicate the need for continuous vigilance and strong political will in addressing the global climate crisis.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the severe catastrophic situations caused by climate change, along with diverse domestic and international efforts to overcome them, and the challenges that still persist. Only sustained attention and action can safeguard the future of humanity. This concludes the climate briefing for September 19, 2026.
